codes.evidence_quote: The flamenca guitar course will cover: 1. The Compás. 2. The Falseta... General technique and study method for the flamenco guitarist.
codes.target: Centro Flamenco Paco Peña seminar curriculum
codes.rationale: The course description frames flamenco guitar knowledge as structured, teachable curriculum with explicit access points for technique, compás, accompaniment, and study method.

possible_but_not_emitted.reason: Named instructors and course organization imply teaching authority, but the visible text mostly lists courses and fees rather than explicitly authorizing a teacher or method.
Compás and technique are named as course topics, but they are not applied as aesthetic criteria for judging flamenco quality in this notice.

annotation_notes: Course listing is mostly administrative, so only the institutional learning-access function is emitted.

codes.evidence_quote: This first workshop will be on choosing and playing castanets. The workshop will be taught by a professional dancer well-versed in the use of castanets.
codes.target: castanet workshop at the May juerga
codes.rationale: The text authorizes instruction through a professional dancer presented as competent to teach castanet choice and technique.

codes.evidence_quote: Bring your instruments, castanets, dance shoes, wear your costumes and plan to participate and have a great time. Any-one with an interest in flamenco and performers at all levels are invited to participate.
codes.rationale: The juerga is framed as an open participatory setting rather than a detached spectator event, with belonging extended through active involvement.

possible_but_not_emitted.reason: The closing remarks praise the prior presentation's atmosphere and support, but the passage is mostly event reporting and lacks sustained critical assessment of artistry.
The text invokes fellowship and local support, but it does not clearly present a community group as possessing authority to judge or sustain flamenco.
Rayna is shown teaching a dance class and speaking on flamenco feeling, but the text is a brief scene report and does not frame her teaching as authorized transmission.
Phrases such as 'unique pictures' and 'active in flamenco dance for many years' are descriptive or lightly promotional rather than clear flamenco critical evaluation.

annotation_notes: Visible text is local-news description with insufficient discourse function for positive coding.

codes.evidence_quote: Paco, in his modest but uncompromising manner, then outlined the workshop as it would be -- "Everyone must have a guitar and everyone must play."
codes.rationale: Paco Peña is positioned as the authority who defines the workshop format and method for learning flamenco guitar.

codes.evidence_quote: "This is the only way one can learn -- one must hold the guitar and try."
codes.rationale: The passage explicitly frames learning as embodied practice through holding the instrument and trying rather than passive observation.

codes.evidence_quote: His criterion for good flamenco is good compás -- it doesn't matter how well developed the technique may be
codes.rationale: Compás is explicitly named as the aesthetic criterion that defines good flamenco, overriding technique alone.

codes.evidence_quote: if it isn't in compás it isn't flamenco, plain and simple
codes.rationale: The statement draws a clear boundary between legitimate flamenco and playing that lacks compás, excluding the latter from flamenco.

possible_but_not_emitted.reason: The workshop gives access to mostly non-flamenco guitarists in an institutional setting, but the stronger evidence concerns Paco Peña's authority and embodied method.
Paco evaluates individual guitarists bluntly, but those judgments mainly serve the pedagogical method and compás criterion already coded.
Paco Peña is treated as a significant artist, but the excerpt does not chiefly construct a canon or ranking of artists.

annotation_notes: The strongest boundary claim is tied to compás as both an aesthetic criterion and a condition for counting as flamenco.
Editorial fundraising and acknowledgments do not contain visible authenticity, pedagogy, community authority, heritage, or critical-evaluative discourse.
